Topic1.Title: Agenda amendment and opening open comment
Topic1.Summary: Council moved to remove item 3D (annexation petition for Cherryville and Murley Lane properties) and add item 3J, a resolution supporting the Boulder County early childhood care and education mill levy and a resolution stating the city's positions on 2026 state ballot measures. The motion passed 8-0. Council then opened open comment and the clerk reviewed participation rules.

Topic2.Title: Open comment: hunting amendment, Gaza, Flat Irons wildfire housing, and taxes
Topic2.Summary: Residents spoke on several subjects. Melinda Marquis opposed Initiative 302, the hunting constitutional amendment on the November ballot. Speakers urged divestment from companies linked to Gaza and Israel and a ceasefire resolution. Walt Morgan asked for a pause on high-density student housing permits in the wildland urban interface because of evacuation risk. Rob Smoke raised divestment and AIPAC, and Lynn Seagull objected to tax increases. Staff said a wildfire home-hardening presentation is planned for August 27.

Topic3.Title: Flock license-plate-reader contract pause
Topic3.Summary: Council members asked about the status of the automated license plate reader (Flock) process. Staff said a pause has been put on the request for proposals, but month-to-month camera use with the current provider continues. Staff said a community engagement plan and additional guardrails for civil liberties and privacy would be shared before any contract is finalized.

Topic4.Title: Consent agenda and bond ballot measure discussion
Topic4.Summary: Council discussed consent agenda items, including ordinance 8758 on a proposed bond measure of more than $400 million. Speakers raised concerns about transparency, community trust, and the budget. Staff said a community advisory panel for capital projects is being considered, and that the city has hired an auditor. Council discussed the Alpine Balsam housing funding and confirmed affordable housing fund money is not going to the Western City campus. The consent agenda passed unanimously.

Topic5.Title: Call-up check-in and suspension of rules for public hearings
Topic5.Summary: The council did not call up item 4A, a landmark alteration certificate to relocate an accessory building at 1733 Canyon Boulevard. Council voted unanimously to suspend procedural rules to allow three public hearings during the meeting.

Topic6.Title: Public hearing: North 30th Street property acquisition (Ordinance 8771)
Topic6.Summary: Transportation staff requested authority to acquire permanent and temporary easements on about 50 properties for the North 30th Street safety improvements project, through negotiation or eminent domain if needed. The project costs about $9.3 million, with a $7.46 million federal grant and $1.87 million in city funds. Council voted unanimously to adopt Ordinance 8771. No public speakers appeared.

Topic7.Title: Public hearing: South 30th Street property acquisition (Ordinance 8772)
Topic7.Summary: Staff requested the same type of property authority for the South 30th Street multimodal improvements project, which connects to Baseline Road and is mostly small temporary easements. The project is about $3.67 million, with a $3 million federal grant and about $670,000 local match. Staff said landscaping on private property would be coordinated with owners and meet zeroscape standards. Council voted unanimously to adopt Ordinance 8772.

Topic8.Title: Public hearing: Sale of KGID-owned parking lot at 2121 Broadway to MALR Boulder LLC
Topic8.Summary: The Downtown Commercial District board considered a purchase agreement to sell the Spruce and Broadway surface lot (59 spaces) to MALR Boulder LLC for a boutique hotel of about 110 rooms, with a proposed price of $5.8 million. The agreement includes 30-year community benefit covenants covering affordable commercial space, public space, arts, local hiring, and energy performance. Staff said a parking study found the lost spaces could be absorbed by nearby garages and that the hotel must still complete full development review. Many residents, churches, and businesses opposed the sale over parking access, while others supported the hotel's economic and vibrancy benefits. The board approved the agreement 7 to 1.

Topic9.Title: Council discussion and water and energy concerns on the hotel
Topic9.Summary: Council members expressed support for the hotel project, while noting the importance of engaging the church and other parking users. Councilmember Taisha raised water supply concerns, noting the 2025 severe-scenario projections were not included, and asked for higher energy and equity standards. Councilmember Rob noted projected revenue from the hotel over 30 years. The motion passed 7 to 1, with one vote against.
